writtenTo: The post-exilic community returning from Babylon
importantNotes: 2 Chronicles 7:14 is one of the most quoted verses on national revival and repentance.
The Chronicler evaluates each king by their faithfulness to God and the Temple.
Good kings include Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, and Josiah — all brought revival.
'The eyes of the LORD range throughout the earth to strengthen those whose hearts are fully committed' (16:9).
The book ends with Cyrus's decree allowing the exiles to return — a note of hope.

chapters.1: Solomon asks God for wisdom at Gibeon; God grants him wisdom and wealth.
chapters.2: Solomon prepares to build the Temple; he arranges labor and materials from Tyre.
chapters.3: Construction of the Temple begins on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem.
chapters.4: The Temple furnishings — the bronze altar, the Sea, lampstands, and courts.
chapters.5: The Ark is brought into the Temple; the glory of the LORD fills the house.
chapters.6: Solomon's prayer of dedication for the Temple.
chapters.7: Fire falls from heaven; God appears to Solomon with the promise of 2 Chronicles 7:14.
chapters.8: Solomon's building projects, administration, and worship organization.
chapters.9: The Queen of Sheba visits; Solomon's wealth and splendor; Solomon's death.
chapters.10: Rehoboam rejects wise counsel; the northern tribes revolt under Jeroboam.
chapters.11: Rehoboam fortifies Judah; the Levites migrate south from the northern kingdom.
chapters.12: Shishak of Egypt invades Judah; Rehoboam humbles himself.
chapters.13: King Abijah defeats Jeroboam's army; his speech appeals to God's covenant.
chapters.14: King Asa's good reign; he defeats a massive Ethiopian army through prayer.
chapters.15: Asa's religious reform encouraged by the prophet Azariah.
chapters.16: Asa relies on Syria instead of God; the prophet Hanani rebukes him.
chapters.17: Jehoshaphat's prosperous and faithful reign; he sends teachers throughout Judah.
chapters.18: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab; the prophet Micaiah warns of defeat.
chapters.19: Jehoshaphat appoints judges and calls for justice throughout Judah.
chapters.20: Jehoshaphat faces a vast army; he prays and God wins the battle through praise.
chapters.21: Jehoram's wicked reign; Edom revolts; Elijah's letter of judgment.
chapters.22: Ahaziah's brief wicked reign; Athaliah seizes the throne after his death.
chapters.23: The priest Jehoiada leads a coup; young Joash is crowned king; Athaliah is executed.
chapters.24: Joash repairs the Temple but turns to idolatry after Jehoiada's death.
chapters.25: Amaziah's mixed reign — victories followed by idolatry and defeat.
chapters.26: Uzziah's prosperous reign; he becomes proud and is struck with leprosy.
chapters.28: Ahaz's wicked reign — he shuts the Temple and worships foreign gods.
chapters.29: Hezekiah reopens and purifies the Temple; worship is restored.
chapters.30: Hezekiah celebrates a great Passover, inviting all Israel and Judah.
chapters.31: Hezekiah organizes the priests and Levites; the people give generously.
chapters.32: Sennacherib threatens Jerusalem; God delivers the city; Hezekiah's later years.
chapters.33: Manasseh's wicked reign; his captivity and repentance; Amon's brief evil reign.
chapters.34: Josiah's great reforms; the Book of the Law is discovered in the Temple.
chapters.35: Josiah celebrates a magnificent Passover; he is killed in battle at Megiddo.
chapters.36: The last kings of Judah; Jerusalem falls to Babylon; Cyrus decrees the return.
